los.text: Describe the main causes, signs, symptoms and pathophysiological process of peripheral nerve injuries (demyelinating vs axonal)
los.html:
InjuryWhat's damagedRecovery
NeurapraxiaConduction block; myelin intact or focal demyelinationWeeks
AxonotmesisAxon cut, sheath intact → Wallerian degenerationRegrows ~1 mm/day
NeurotmesisWhole nerve cutNeeds surgical repair
DemyelinatingAxonal
PathologySchwann cell/myelin damageAxon degeneration ("dying back", length-dependent)
Nerve conductionSlowed velocity, conduction block, prolonged distal latencyReduced amplitude, velocity near normal
ClinicalEarly global areflexia, proximal + distal weaknessDistal "glove and stocking" sensory loss first, distal wasting, ankle jerks lost first
ExamplesGBS (AIDP), CIDP, CMT1Diabetes, alcohol, B12, drugs (vincristine), CMT2, vasculitis
SymptomsPositive (tingling, burning pain) and negative (numbness, weakness); autonomic (postural hypotension, erectile dysfunction, gastroparesis).
Signs (LMN)Wasting, hypotonia, weakness, ↓/absent reflexes, fasciculations, sensory loss in a nerve/root/length-dependent pattern.
PatternsMononeuropathy (compression/trauma), mononeuritis multiplex (vasculitis, diabetes), polyneuropathy (metabolic/toxic).

los.text: Describe the main causes, clinical features and principles of investigation and treatment of common compression neuropathies, acute polyneuropathy (Guillain-Barré syndrome), shingles and chronic sensory peripheral neuropathy
sessions: Clin 2: Clinically important neuropathies: Presentation, pathology and treatment
los.html:
Compression neuropathies
  • Carpal tunnel (median): nocturnal tingling thumb–index–middle–half ring, thenar wasting (APB weakness), Tinel's/Phalen's. Associations: pregnancy, hypothyroid, RA, diabetes, acromegaly. Rx: wrist splint, steroid injection, surgical decompression.
  • Ulnar (cubital tunnel): little/ring finger tingling, interossei wasting, Froment's sign, claw hand.
  • Common peroneal (fibular head; leg crossing, casts): foot drop, ↓ dorsiflexion and eversion, sensory loss on dorsum of foot.
  • Radial (spiral groove, "Saturday night palsy"): wrist drop.
Guillain–Barré syndrome
  • Post-infectious (Campylobacter, CMV, EBV) molecular mimicry → acute ascending symmetrical weakness, areflexia, mild sensory symptoms, back pain, autonomic instability.
  • Nadir within 4 weeks.
  • Ix: NCS (demyelination), CSF high protein, normal cells (albuminocytological dissociation), anti-ganglioside antibodies (anti-GQ1b in Miller Fisher).
  • Monitor FVC (respiratory failure → ITU).
  • Rx: IVIg or plasma exchange
  • VTE prophylaxis.
  • Steroids don't help.
Shingles (herpes zoster)
  • VZV reactivation in dorsal root/cranial ganglion → pain then dermatomal vesicular rash.
  • Rx: aciclovir/valaciclovir within 72 h (always if ophthalmic).
  • Postherpetic neuralgia → amitriptyline, gabapentinoids, lidocaine plasters.
  • Vaccine (Shingrix) offered from 65 (UK).
Chronic sensory peripheral neuropathy
  • Diabetes (commonest), alcohol, B12 deficiency, hypothyroidism, CKD, drugs, paraprotein.
  • Ix: glucose/HbA1c, B12/folate, TFTs, U&E, LFTs, serum electrophoresis.
  • Rx: treat cause, foot care, neuropathic pain agents (amitriptyline, duloxetine, gabapentin, pregabalin).

los.text: Describe the main clinical features and principles of treatment and management of migraine and cluster headache
los.html:
MigraineCluster headache
WhoF>M, young adults, FHxM>F, 20–40, smokers
PainUnilateral pulsating, moderate–severe, 4–72 hSevere unilateral orbital/temporal, 15–180 min, up to 8/day, often at night
FeaturesNausea, photophobia, phonophobia; worse with activity; ± aura (visual, sensory, <60 min)Ipsilateral autonomic: lacrimation, red eye, rhinorrhoea, ptosis/miosis; restless/agitated
PatternEpisodic triggers (menses, sleep, food, stress)Clusters lasting weeks, then remission
Acute RxSimple analgesia/NSAID + triptan ± antiemetic; avoid opioids100% O₂ (12–15 L/min) + SC/nasal sumatriptan
PreventionPropranolol, topiramate (teratogenic), amitriptyline; candesartan; CGRP antibodies if refractoryVerapamil (ECG monitoring); steroids bridging
Pathophysiology of migraineTrigeminovascular activation, CGRP release, cortical spreading depression (aura).
Medication overuse headacheAnalgesics ≥15 days/month or triptans/opioids ≥10 days/month → withdraw.
Combined hormonal contraception contraindicated in migraine with aura (stroke risk).
Triptans(5-HT1B/1D agonists)Avoid in IHD, uncontrolled HTN.

los.text: Explain how information is transferred in an individual nerve cell and how the nervous system communicates from cell to cell
los.html:
Resting membrane potential(~ −70 mV)Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase (3 Na⁺ out, 2 K⁺ in) + K⁺ leak channels.
Action potential
  • Threshold (~ −55 mV) → voltage-gated Na⁺ channels open (depolarisation) → Na⁺ channels inactivate + voltage-gated K⁺ channels open (repolarisation, hyperpolarisation).
  • All-or-none.
  • Refractory periods (absolute, relative) ensure one-way propagation.
Propagation
  • Continuous in unmyelinated fibres
  • Saltatory between nodes of Ranvier in myelinated fibres (faster; Schwann cells in PNS, oligodendrocytes in CNS).
  • Speed ↑ with diameter and myelination.
Synaptic transmission
  • AP reaches terminal
  • → voltage-gated Ca²⁺ influx
  • → vesicle fusion (SNARE proteins; blocked by botulinum toxin)
  • → neurotransmitter release
  • → binds postsynaptic receptors: ionotropic (fast, e.g. nicotinic, GABA-A, AMPA) or metabotropic (GPCR, slower, e.g. muscarinic).
  • Produces EPSPs or IPSPs, which summate (spatial, temporal) at the axon hillock.
TerminationEnzymatic breakdown (AChE), reuptake (SERT, NET, DAT), diffusion.
Electrical synapsesGap junctions (fast, bidirectional).

los.text: Describe the anatomy of the autonomic nervous system (ANS) and the pathways taken by the ANS to and from the CNS
los.html:
Sympathetic (thoracolumbar, T1–L2)
  • Preganglionic cell bodies in lateral horn
  • → ventral root
  • → white rami communicantes
  • → paravertebral sympathetic chain (synapse, or ascend/descend)
  • → postganglionic fibres via grey rami to spinal nerves (skin, vessels, sweat glands) or as splanchnic nerves to prevertebral ganglia (coeliac, superior and inferior mesenteric) for gut.
  • Short preganglionic, long postganglionic. Adrenal medulla = modified ganglion (receives preganglionic fibres directly).
  • Head via superior cervical ganglion (Horner's syndrome if disrupted).
Parasympathetic (craniosacral)
  • Cranial nerves III (ciliary ganglion → pupil constriction, accommodation)
  • VII (pterygopalatine and submandibular ganglia → lacrimal, submandibular, sublingual glands)
  • IX (otic ganglion → parotid)
  • X (thoracic and abdominal viscera to the splenic flexure) and S2–S4 pelvic splanchnics (hindgut, bladder, erection).
  • Long preganglionic, short postganglionic (ganglia in/near organs).
AfferentsVisceral sensory fibres travel with autonomic nerves (e.g. vagal afferents to NTS; pain with sympathetics → referred pain).
Central controlHypothalamus, brainstem (NTS, vasomotor centre), limbic system.
Enteric nervous systemMyenteric and submucosal plexuses, modulated by ANS.

los.text: Explain the functions and control of the autonomic nervous system (including receptor types)
los.html:
Sympathetic("fight or flight")↑ HR and contractility, bronchodilation, mydriasis, ↑ glycogenolysis/lipolysis, vasoconstriction (skin, gut) and vasodilation (skeletal muscle), ↓ gut motility, sphincter contraction, sweating, ejaculation.
Parasympathetic("rest and digest")↓ HR, bronchoconstriction, miosis and accommodation, ↑ salivation and gut secretion/motility, sphincter relaxation, bladder emptying, erection.
ReceptorTransmitterLocation / effect
Nicotinic (Nn)AChAll autonomic ganglia, adrenal medulla (ligand-gated ion channel)
Muscarinic M2AChHeart: ↓ HR, ↓ AV conduction (Gi)
Muscarinic M3AChSmooth muscle contraction, glands, bladder detrusor, pupil (Gq)
α1NAVasoconstriction, pupil dilation, bladder neck/prostate contraction (Gq)
α2NAPresynaptic inhibition of NA release; central (↓ sympathetic outflow) (Gi)
β1NA/AdrHeart ↑ rate/force; renin release (Gs)
β2AdrBronchodilation, vasodilation (muscle), uterine relaxation, glycogenolysis, K⁺ into cells (Gs)
β3NALipolysis, detrusor relaxation (Gs)
ExceptionSympathetic fibres to sweat glands release ACh (muscarinic).
ControlDual innervation with tonic activity; reflexes via hypothalamus and brainstem (baroreflex, micturition reflex).
